Assessment of BA.evidence_source: Participants completed the 10-item Body Acceptance by Others Scale (BAOS; Avalos & Tylka, 2006), a measure of an individual's perceptions of feeling acceptance for, and receiving messages reflecting acceptance of, their body shape and weight from five external sources (friends, family, dating partners, society, and the media; sample item: ''I've felt acceptance from my friends regarding my body shape and/or weight'').
Assessment of BA.warning: BAOS is not one of the allowed values (allowed: 'BAS', 'BAS-2'); therefore extract_value set to None per schema rules.

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the 10-item Body Acceptance by Others Scale (BAOS; Avalos & Tylka, 2006), including its items, 5-point response scale, scoring (mean of items), and prior psychometric support among US adults. It also reports internal consistency in the current sample: Cronbach's alpha = .90 for women and .92 for men. The section does not state the study label, sample size, country of the current sample, survey method, BMI assessment, or correlations with BMI.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: 'Participants completed the 10-item Body Acceptance by Others Scale (BAOS; Avalos & Tylka, 2006)... Participants rated the frequency of these experiences using a 5-point scale, ranging from 1 (Never) to 5 (Always). An overall score was computed as the mean of all items... Among US adults, BAOS scores have been found to have a one-dimensional factor structure, good test–retest reliability after 3 weeks, and good patterns of construct validity (Avalos & Tylka, 2006). Here, Cronbach's a for this scale was .90 in women and .92 in men.'
